title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the deposited crystal structure 9Y1T (503,881-byte mmCIF): one 145-residue protein chain with Rhodamine 101 bound, 2.7 Angstrom resolution, released 2026-09-09; confirmed 9Y1S (apo form) is also released and downloadable. Read the open preprint full text (PMC12262669) including its data availability statement. Confirmed by direct query that no Zenodo deposit exists for 'Rhobin' (0 hits), no code repository exists (3 unrelated GitHub hits), the paper DOI returns no Zenodo/Dryad record, and a full-text Protein Data Bank search for 'Rhobin' returns only one unrelated entry. Crossref shows the version of record is CC BY-NC 4.0.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The counts of designs and dyes: nine designed proteins (Rhobin1-Rhobin9) and roughly seven named rhodamine dyes (JF660, JFX650, JF646, JFX646, SiRh101, SiRhP, THQ-FSiRh). The dissociation constants (strongest 57 nanomolar for Rhobin9 with JF660), melting temperatures (all above 95 degrees Celsius), and brightness values, which sit in supplementary PDF tables S1-S6. The bioRxiv supplementary PDF itself returned HTTP 429 and HTTP 403 and was not retrieved, so the table contents are from the main text's descriptions only.

a1_downloadable.note: Two crystal structures download freely from the Protein Data Bank (I opened 9Y1T) and the article is CC BY-NC 4.0, but no numeric data table is deposited anywhere: no Zenodo, no code repo, and the availability statement covers only plasmids ('available from Addgene ... or upon request').

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The candidate labels (dissociation constant in nanomolar, molecular brightness, melting temperature) are reported measured values, not constructed by joining. Caveat: they live in supplementary PDF tables and would need hand transcription, which is cheap only because there are so few of them.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are obtainable (I read the 145-residue Rhobin9 sequence out of the 9Y1T structure file). Dye structures are drawn as pictures, so SMILES (text chemical structures) would be looked up for about seven named commercial dyes, which is trivial at that scale.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit in the text: dissociation constants in nanomolar, melting temperatures in degrees Celsius, resolution in Angstroms.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. Nine designed proteins against roughly seven rhodamine dyes is at most about 63 protein-dye measurements, and the paper itself says the designs were made 'in a one-shot manner by testing only a handful of sequences'. No screening library, no site-saturation mutagenesis, no high-throughput sort. That is one to two orders of magnitude below the ~400-row classification floor and ~1,500-row regression floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <2 MB (two mmCIF structures plus a few dozen numbers)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; size is the opposite of this paper's problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nine designs is consistent across the preprint main text and the Cell abstract. The number of RFdiffusion backbones and LigandMPNN sequences generated and filtered is never reported, so the design funnel (and hence any failure set) cannot be reconstructed.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are genuine physical measurements: fluorescence titration for affinity, circular dichroism for thermal stability, spectroscopy for brightness. Not another model's output and not computable from the features.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for the binder sequence plus ChemBERTa (molecule language model) for the dye, if the data existed
backbone.hardware: CPU would be ample at this scale
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT, ChemBERTa permissive; not the limiting factor here

integration.partner_dataset: Protein Data Bank entries for other fluorogen-activating proteins, plus the companion designed fluorophore-binder papers (orthogonal far-red/orange/green binders, Science 2026; the Rhb-Me Zenodo deposits)
integration.join_key: PDB ID and dye identity (InChIKey once SMILES are drawn)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Pooling every published designed fluorophore-binder could in principle ask which pocket geometries turn a dye's bright state on, but the pool would still be in the low hundreds of pairs and assembled from incomparable assays across labs.

controls.positive_control: None runnable: with nine designs there is no held-out set in which to recover a known effect.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=9.
controls.external_validation: Other designed fluorophore-binder papers exist (e.g. the 2026 orthogonal far-red/orange/green binder work), but their affinities come from different assays and would not be comparable.

honest_claim_h3: With nine designed proteins and about seven dyes, any model could only claim it interpolates a roughly 9-by-7 table of measurements that the authors already report in full, which is a lookup table, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a designed protein's sequence and a dye's chemical structure to predict how tightly they bind and how brightly the dye glows.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on pairs of (designed binder protein, rhodamine dye). Verified count: 9 proteins and about 7 dyes, so at most roughly 63 pairs.
plain_idea.predict: Binding strength (dissociation constant, in nanomolar) and fluorescence brightness gain, measured by fluorescence titration of purified protein against dye in a cuvette.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Protein designers currently test designs one at a time in the lab; a model ranking designs before synthesis would save weeks per round. But this paper supplies far too few measurements to fit or test one.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict rhodamine-binding affinity and fluorogenicity for de novo designed pockets from protein sequence or structure plus dye chemistry, using frozen ESM-2 and ChemBERTa embeddings with a small regression head. The paper is a nine-design success story, not a dataset: there is no screening library, no mutational scan, and no deposited measurement table, so the whole label set is a few dozen numbers printed in a supplementary PDF. Its two crystal structures (9Y1S apo, 9Y1T with Rhodamine 101) are genuinely useful as structural input features for someone else's larger fluorogen-binder dataset, and that is the only ML-relevant asset here.

effort.compute_note: Everything here is trivial to compute because the dataset is tiny: two structure files totalling about 1 MB (one of which I downloaded and timed implicitly in seconds) and a few dozen measurements that would be typed in by hand. Not timed beyond the structure download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled protein-dye pairs. Done: nine designed proteins times roughly seven dyes, at most about 63, and the paper states only 'a handful of sequences' were ever tested. This killed the project in one step.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 decisively: nine designed proteins and about seven dyes give at most ~63 measurements, with no screening library, no mutational scan, and no deposited data table (only two crystal structures and Addgene plasmids). It is an excellent protein-engineering result and a non-dataset for machine learning.
